inference: Persistent reads rebuild a polynomial and clone each radical Vec. Share only the rational/radical array through an optional Arc<Vec>, using copy-on-write for mutation and unwrapping or cloning on consuming iteration. The prior diagnostic counts cache copies, not allocation counts, time share or expected savings.
ownership: Opaque atom Vecs and polynomial term Vecs retain their original cloning and ownership. The shared array owns only Rational pairs. Mutable access uses Arc::make_mut before exposing entries; consuming access uses Arc::unwrap_or_clone. No unsafe implementation, static memo, lock escape or expression-node owner is introduced.
rational_caveat: Sharing the array changes Rational reference-count traffic. Rational ownership-sensitive paths were inspected: unique negation or extraction cannot mutate a shared live array because mutable and consuming storage access first obtains owned entries. Qualification still checks every admitted P4 test and exact witnesses; numerical cache costs and retention are measured rather than assumed identical.
cost_risk: A new nonempty buffer allocates both a Vec payload and an Arc header; mutations of shared buffers copy. Empty storage is None and mutable empty iteration allocates nothing. Reference-count operations, retained capacity, first-query and construction costs can offset cheaper read copies. Smaller struct layouts are not proof of lower total memory.
